messages:
sam (sales): heads-up — FinLedger verbally agreed to an enterprise commit. They quoted 1.5M tokens/day with SLO 99.9% and want details on capacity plan, preheat, and pricing. traffic shape: steady ~20 rps, bursts up to 200 rps for 3–5m, avg seq len ~256, workload mix chat: 70% / embeddings: 30%. they also flagged the security questionnaire as a blocker. can eng advise on reserved GPU profile + autoscale policy?
maria (sales-eng): thanks. couple quick q's: 1) burst concurrency vs rps — are bursts concurrent short spikes or many short requests? 2) do they require cross-AZ failover? 3) any expectation for cold-start latency (<100ms?)
alex (eng-infra): @maria good call. from ops perspective: we need peak concurrency and per-request token distribution. but rough thought: steady 20 rps -> small pool. bursts 200 rps for 5m means headroom for 10x. also need to know if embeddings traffic is large batches (multi-request) or inline.
jordan (eng-runtime): rough recommendation based on provided shape: reserve a Dedicated pool sized for baseline + some headroom: baseline = 20 rps at seq 256 -> ~2 GPUs (A100-80GB equiv) for consistent latency. For bursts to 200 rps, either: 1) reserve 4 GPUs + burst credits for short spikes, or 2) reserve 2 GPUs + autoscale to 8 GPUs with fast prewarm. Option 1 simpler for SLA; option 2 cheaper but needs preheat policy and burst-credit config.
amelia (sales-eng): oops typo — maria here. jordan, can you share a sample autoscale policy we can give them? and any notes on expected token cost delta when autoscaling?
jordan (eng-runtime): sure — sample (pseudoyaml):

```
autoscale_policy:
  min_replicas: 2
  target_rps_per_gpu: 50
  max_replicas: 8
  burst_window_seconds: 300
  burst_headroom_percent: 25
  prewarm_on_scale: true
```

Notes: target_rps_per_gpu depends on model variant and quantization; 50 rps/gpu is conservative for chat seq=256 on high perf kernels. Burst_window_seconds=300 matches their 3–5m bursts. burst_headroom keeps spare capacity during scaling. prewarm_on_scale reduces cold-starts but needs warm pool or faster startup images.
katie (security): on the security questionnaire: they asked about KMS integration & key custody, SOC2, and network isolation. we can confirm: KMS via customer-managed keys (CloudKMS/HSM) supported on Private and Dedicated with our standard contract clause. for Hosted we can offer envelope encryption but not customer-controlled HSM unless Private. need to flag this in the sales doc.
maria (sales-eng): thanks. for pricing: if they take option 1 (reserve 4 GPUs) what discount band should we present? and if option 2 (reserve 2 + autoscale) how do we price burst usage?
alex (eng-infra): simple pricing guidance: reserved GPU monthly commit pricing band 20–30% off list depending on term. autoscale bursts billed as usage on top of reservation; we recommend a burst credit pool for enterprise commits — e.g., include N GPU-hours/mo for free, additional billed at spot/usage rate with a cap. ops can model expected cost once we have the exact token mix.
jordan (eng-runtime): also note: prefix/KV cache effectiveness will reduce GPU needs for chat-heavy workloads if many sessions share context. if FinLedger has many repeat sessions we can recommend caching policy to lower steady GPU count.
sam (sales): great — action items: 1) @jordan produce a short doc with recommended reserve sizes and the YAML autoscale snippet + expected latencies per option. 2) @katie write the definitive KMS/network answer we can include in the questionnaire (short paragraph + contract language). 3) ops (alex) to draft a pricing addendum example: reserve-4 vs reserve-2+burst credit. target to share with customer by EOD tomorrow.
ops-bot: reminder: please attach estimated cost calc to the thread before EOD. :bell:

maria (sales-eng): ping — i'll consolidate into the proposal once we have those pieces. :thumbsup:
